title: Cross-shard prefix-stable eviction contract and continuous-batching integration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: GPU memory pressure and continuous-batching interactions lead to non-deterministic prefix eviction that can cause stale KV hits, incorrect cache pin lifetimes, and tail-latency spikes. Goal: define a cross-shard, prefix-aware eviction contract that is compatible with continuous batching and GPU slab allocations, with a clear correctness spec (prefix-stable linearizability), an implementation plan that minimizes throughput regressions, and a robust test/fuzz harness for verification.
design_decisions: Define 'prefix-stable linearizability' as the core correctness invariant: once a prefix is served with KV entries present, subsequent requests that extend that prefix must not observe evicted entries unless a canonical invalidation event occurs.
Use lease tokens (small, monotonic integers) attached to cache pins; evictors must compare lease tokens to ensure in-flight batched requests do not drop required prefixes mid-batch.

Hybrid eviction strategy: LRU baseline + per-prefix TTL + 'pin bump' for recently used prefixes; eviction rank = weighted(LRU_score, TTL_slack, prefix_hotness). Weights are tunable by runtime-profiled heuristics.

Cross-shard coordination uses lightweight epoch markers instead of full consensus: each shard advertises an epoch counter and a compact eviction watermark for prefixes it owns. Global coordinator computes safe eviction watermarks per prefix-range while respecting continuous-batching windows.
GPU memory optimization: perform slab-aware eviction that prefers demotion to smaller quantized buffers before full eviction to reduce fragmentation and avoid OOMs during large batch spikes.

Fallbacks: When coordination latency or memory pressure is high, automatically fall back to conservative per-shard retention (increase TTL) to avoid correctness violations at the expense of higher memory usage.
Expose runtime knobs in Console: eviction-profile, epoch-sync-interval, slab-demote-threshold, batch-affinity-window for targeted rollouts.
Instrumentation-first approach: every eviction decision must emit an event with prefix, shard, epoch, reason, lease_token, and pre/post memory snapshot for post-mortem and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Formal spec document for 'prefix-stable linearizability' reviewed and approved by runtime and reliability teams (link in links).
Implementation produces zero observed prefix-stability regressions in synthetic canary workloads (defined below).
No more than 5% regression in aggregate throughput for standard batching workloads at P50/P95 under typical traffic profile when compared to baseline runtime-1.23.
Automated property-based tests and chaos scenarios pass in CI for both single-shard and cross-shard setups.

Dashboard panels added to Console monitoring: eviction-miss-rate, prefix-stability-violations, slab-fragmentation-index, and batch-induced-eviction-counts. Alerts wired for >0 prefix-stability violations in canary namespace.
Rollout plan validated with blue/green canary and an automatic rollback on detection of correctness violations or >10% customer-impacting error increase.
implementation_steps: Write the formal spec and invariants (doc/srv/prefix-stability.md) and circulate for review (1 week).
Add lease token field to cache pin APIs and wire through continuous-batching path (runtime change + SDK compatibility shim).
Implement hybrid eviction scoring function inside shard-local evictor and add slab-demote path that creates compacted quantized buffers instead of immediate eviction.
Implement epoch advertisement and compact watermark exchange in shard heartbeat; coordinator computes candidate evictions and returns safe watermarks.
Add conservative fallback that increases TTL and disables demotion when coordination lag > threshold.
Add comprehensive observability events for every eviction decision and integrate with Console dashboards.
Benchmark memory/throughput impact on internal perf harness (small/medium/large models) and iterate on weights for scoring function.
Hook up property-based tests and end-to-end chaos tests in CI and run nightly fuzzing across GPU-backed clusters.
Prepare rollout pipeline (canary namespace, 10% traffic, 50% GPU capacity shadowing) and automated rollback triggers.
testing_and_validation: Property tests: invariants checker that replays recorded request traces and asserts prefix-stability under simulated evictions.
Fuzz harness: random sequence generator that interleaves batching windows, lease renewals, shard restarts, and OOM signals. Run for 24h in CI smoke and 72h in nightly.
Chaos scenarios: network partition between coordinator and shards, delayed epoch adverts, simulated large-batch spike during compaction, and forced slab fragmentation events.

Canary workload: synthetic traces built from customer traces (anonymized) that include long-prefix conversations and short queries. Metrics: prefix-stability-violations == 0, eviction-miss-rate < 2% in steady state.
GPU OOM simulation: synthetic memory pressure to confirm demote->evict path prevents OOM more often than baseline (target: 3x reduction in forced restarts during bursts).
Performance regression tests: run p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput across small, medium, large model configs with baseline and feature flags on/off.
Review of logs and structured eviction events to ensure every 'in-flight' decision contains lease_token and epoch fields for traceability.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy coordinator and telemetry changes to staging cluster; enable verbose eviction logs and run smoke tests (1 week)
Stage 2: enable hybrid eviction with conservative weights in canary namespace (10% of traffic) for 72 hours, monitor prefix-stability and memory metrics.
Stage 3: expand to 50% traffic and enable slab-demote path; run night-long fuzzing and increased load tests.
Stage 4: full rollout to runtime-1.24 with gradual weight tuning (2-3 days) and continuous monitoring; keep automatic rollback for 48 hours.
Emergency rollback criteria: any detected prefix-stability violation in customer-facing namespaces or >10% increase in 5xx errors over baseline.
